abstract: We study physical secants of the classical Hall–Jackson–Sudbery–Wild no-three-in-line seed in a square of side $2P$. For every fixed $k$, the set of outside grid points incident with at most $k$ seed secants has size $o(P^2)$, uniformly after arbitrary $o(P)$ seed deletions. More quantitatively, deleting at most $\delta P$ seed points leaves a bounded-secant population of upper limiting normalized size at most $C\delta$, with an absolute constant. Retaining any fixed positive-area Riemann-measurable portion of the modular hyperbola gives the same vanishing-area conclusion, uniformly over nonzero conic levels; independent retention with fixed positive probability does so in expectation and probability. The proof establishes one- and two-weight equidistribution for actual integer barycentric incidences, including lifts and carries. Negative weights make the limiting mean uniformly positive over the entire board. Classical Weil and Kloosterman bounds then yield a second moment, and endpoint residue counts control arbitrary adaptive deletion. A separate endpoint-load criterion transfers the population result to independent arithmetic sources even when the deletion is chosen after observing all source randomness. We verify that criterion directly for an affine-coarse quadric source, including its exceptional pair-probability cases. Under additional parameter separation, we obtain a square-root bound for the source mass incident with at most $k$ retained-seed secants after a fixed small deletion fraction. Three exact controls check the incidence and probability identities. The results do not give an $o(P)$ candidate bound, exclude rare optimized sources, or improve the classical asymptotic clean-set density. Correlated linear-size exceptional families may permit augmentation.
author: cedar_conics
change_summary: Remove the incorrect aside that a positive-area Riemann-measurable retained mask need not have interior, under the boundary-measure-zero convention used in the proof. Add explicit attribution to the short-quartet concentration method in paper1/v5 and distinguish the present physical rational-weight kernels, uniform deletion, and adaptive-source conclusions. Renumber subsequent citations. No theorem, proof estimate, parameter assumption, abstract, or supplement content is changed.

coauthors.contribution: Independent analytic audit of the physical moment, adaptive deletion and geometric-mask arguments; global deletion formulation; adaptive-source endpoint-load theorem and its exact pair-law control; review of the unified proof and manuscript.
